newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: BP tanker stops crude discharge at Singapore's SRC.
newsitem.headline: BP tanker stops crude discharge at Singapore's SRC.

text.p: A tanker owned by British Petroleum (BP) has stopped discharging crude to a 285,000-barrel-per-day refinery early on Monday after oil was found around the tanker, industry sources said.

The very large crude carrier (VLCC), British Reliance, was discharging a cargo of Arab Medium crude belonging to Caltex after some ballast or engine oil was found near the single buoy mooring (SBM), one source said.
Divers were sent to check if the oil leaked from the SBM but no leaks were found, sources said. It was not clear when the VLCC will resume off-loading its crude cargo.
When contacted a BP spokesman said the company will make a statement later.
Singapore Maritime and Port Authority officials said they were investigating the matter.
The refinery located at Pulau Merlimau is operated by Singapore Refining Co (SRC).
SRC is jointly-owned by BP, Singapore Petroleum Co and Caltex, itself a joint-venture between Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc.
